title: [CQ-R11e3a] Lockfile registry entry admission
definitionOfDone: admitLockfiles admits only lockfileVersion 2/3 entries at node_modules locations whose resolved is exactly the canonical https://registry.npmjs.org tarball URL for their name and version, with one canonical sha512 integrity. Every other kind throws its fixed DEPENDENCY_* code: link, git, file, http, another host, userinfo/port/query/fragment, alias-to-tarball, missing/sha1/multi-hash/non-canonical integrity, and a non-node_modules key. Shown by the DA rows.

Root and inBundle entries are skipped, and so are optional entries whose os excludes linux or whose cpu excludes the given cpu (npm list semantics; libc is never filtered). Every other entry is admitted once per distinct integrity, in a deeply frozen result that does not depend on input order. Shown by the DA rows.
Input, lockfile-size, lockfile-count and package-count bounds refuse with fixed codes, and no error message carries a URL, path or lockfile byte. Shown by the DA rows.

dependency-cache.mjs imports only node:buffer/node:crypto-style built-ins and ./source-snapshot.mjs, with no fs, network or child_process. It admits the repository's own packages/moe-daemon/package-lock.json. Shown by a DA row.
The verification command exits 0, with its output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (red). Load test-driven-development.

Work in scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs:
- Append a 'CQ-R11e3a lockfile admission' section after the C rows.
- Put its imports in the file's top import block: admitLockfiles, dependencyError, MAX_LOCKFILES, MAX_LOCKFILE_BYTES and MAX_DEPENDENCY_PACKAGES from '../local-runner/dependency-cache.mjs', and MAX_IMPORT_ENTRIES from '../local-runner/source-snapshot.mjs'.
- Reuse caught() and the file's existing helpers.
- Rows are DA1-DA5. Grep `test('DA` first.
- The global forbidden patterns apply to test strings too. Never write the double-underscore proto literal; use 'constructor' or 'toString' for prototype-key inputs.

Helpers (small):
- sri(seed) = 'sha512-' + base64(sha512(seed)).
- url(name, version = '1.0.0') = `https://registry.npmjs.org/${name}/-/${name.split('/').pop()}-${version}.tgz`.
- ok(name, extra) = {version: '1.0.0', resolved: url(name), integrity: sri(name), ...extra}.
- lock(packages, lockfileVersion = 3) = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({lockfileVersion, packages: {'': {name: 'fixture'}, ...packages}})).
- admit(lockfiles, cpu = 'x64') = admitLockfiles({lockfiles, cpu}).
- refused(fn, code) asserts three things: the thrown error's code; that its message equals dependencyError(code).message; and that the message contains none of the row's distinctive input text (the URL host, the key, the dir, the integrity).

DA1. Input refusals, each DEPENDENCY_INPUT_INVALID:
- The input is null, an array, a string, or a record with an extra key or without cpu.
- cpu is 'ia32', 'X64', 'x86_64', 1, or new String('x64').
- lockfiles is not an array, an Array subclass, [], 17 valid records, or a Proxy over an array whose length is 1e9 or whose get trap throws.
- An element is a non-record, has an extra key, or has no bytes.
- dir is '', '/abs', '../x', 'a/../b', './x', '.moe/x', or 'a\\b'; or dirs are duplicated: ['.', '.'] and ['sub', 'sub'].
- bytes is a string, an ArrayBuffer, a DataView, a Uint16Array, or 7.
- A getter on cpu throws: the result is the fixed refusal, not the getter's error.
A counting getter proves that cpu, lockfiles, each element, dir and bytes are each read exactly once on a SUCCESSFUL call.

DA2. Lockfile refusals, each DEPENDENCY_LOCKFILE_INVALID:
- an invalid UTF-8 byte INSIDE a JSON string ('{"a":"<0xff>"}'), which proves fatal decoding matters;
- non-JSON text;
- JSON null, an array or a number;
- lockfileVersion 1, '3' (a string), 4, or missing;
- packages missing, null, an array, or a string;
- a packages entry that is 5 or null.
A UTF-8 BOM before a valid lockfile is accepted, as npm's JSON parsing accepts it.

DA3. Entry refusals. Each lockfile has a VALID entry first and then the bad one; assert the exact code with refused().
- DEPENDENCY_LOCATION_INVALID, for each of these keys: 'src/x', 'node_modules', 'node_modules/', 'node_modules/@s', 'node_modules/@s/', 'node_modules/a/b', 'node_modules/../x', 'node_modules/./x', 'node_modules/.bin', 'node_modules/_x', 'node_modules/a/node_modules', 'node_modules/a//node_modules/b', 'packages/ws', 'node_modules/a\\b', 'node_modules/a b', 'node_modules/%2e%2e'.
- DEPENDENCY_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED for:
  - link:true;
  - resolved values 'git+https://github.com/x/a.git#abc', 'git+ssh://git@github.com/x/a.git', 'file:../a', 'http://registry.npmjs.org/a/-/a-1.0.0.tgz' and 'https://registry.yarnpkg.com/a/-/a-1.0.0.tgz';
  - the userinfo form 'https://u:p@registry.npmjs.org/...' and the port form 'https://registry.npmjs.org:443/...';
  - a '?x=1' suffix, a '#x' suffix, and an uppercase 'REGISTRY.npmjs.org' host;
  - alias-to-tarball: location node_modules/a, no name, resolved url('b');
  - a version mismatch: version '1.0.0' with resolved url('a', '1.0.1');
  - missing resolved, missing version, version 'latest', version '1.0';
  - name '../x', and name 5.
- DEPENDENCY_INTEGRITY_INVALID for:
  - a missing integrity;
  - 'sha1-...' and 'sha256-...';
  - '<valid sha512> sha1-...' (multi-hash);
  - an 85-char body; the 86 chars without '=='; a leading space; 'SHA512-...';
  - NON-CANONICAL base64: the canonical text with the character before '==' changed only in its padding bits, so it decodes to the same 64 bytes.

DA4. Acceptance and skips. Use a v2 lockfile at dir 'sub' and a v3 lockfile at dir '.':
- The root '' entry has a garbage resolved and is skipped.
- These are admitted: a scoped '@s/b'; a nested 'node_modules/a/node_modules/c'; and an npm alias, location node_modules/alias with name 'real' and resolved url('real').
- An inBundle entry with no resolved and no integrity is skipped.
- Optional entries:
  - os ['darwin']: skipped;
  - os ['!win32'], os 'linux' (a string) and os ['any']: admitted;
  - cpu ['arm64']: skipped for cpu 'x64', admitted for 'arm64';
  - cpu ['!arm64']: admitted for x64, skipped for arm64;
  - libc ['musl']: admitted.
- A NON-optional entry with os ['darwin'] and a devOptional (not optional) one are both admitted.
- The same integrity at two locations and in both lockfiles gives ONE package whose url is the smaller canonical URL.
- The result deepEquals the expected {dirs: ['.', 'sub'], packages: [...sorted by sha512]}, every sha512 is 128 lowercase hex, and the result, dirs, packages and each package are all Object.isFrozen.
- Reversing lockfiles and the insertion order of packages keys gives a deepEqual result.
- dirs ['b', 'a', '.'] come back as ['.', 'a', 'b'].

DA5. Bounds and a real lockfile:
- MAX_LOCKFILES === 16, MAX_LOCKFILE_BYTES === 16_777_216, and MAX_DEPENDENCY_PACKAGES === MAX_IMPORT_ENTRIES - 1.
- A valid lockfile padded with trailing spaces to MAX_LOCKFILE_BYTES + 1 bytes gives DEPENDENCY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Padded to exactly MAX_LOCKFILE_BYTES, it is admitted.
- A generated lockfile with MAX_DEPENDENCY_PACKAGES + 1 distinct packages (names 'p<i>', integrities sri('p<i>')) gives DEPENDENCY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Exactly MAX_DEPENDENCY_PACKAGES is admitted, and so are two lockfiles that each hold the same MAX.
- readFileSync of packages/moe-daemon/package-lock.json is admitted with cpu 'x64'. packages is non-empty, every url starts with 'https://registry.npmjs.org/', and every sha512 is 128 lowercase hex.

Run the file. It must fail to load with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for dependency-cache.mjs, which is red for the right reason. No E, K or C row is edited.

implementationPlan.description:
Create scripts/local-runner/dependency-cache.mjs: pure lockfile admission.

Imports: only validateImportPath and MAX_IMPORT_ENTRIES from './source-snapshot.mjs'. Buffer and TextDecoder are globals. Use no fs, net, http, child_process or dynamic import.

DoD 4's import clause describes this slice. CQ-R11e3 later adds node:fs/promises, node:path and the shared downloader to this module for buildDependencyCache. admitLockfiles' own call graph must stay pure, with no I/O.

Header comment:
- the purpose: admission before any download, for the offline check cache;
- the trust model: candidate lockfiles are untrusted;
- the rules below;
- that libc is deliberately not filtered;
- that workspaces and links are refused;
- that messages are fixed text.

Exports:
- MAX_LOCKFILES = 16, MAX_LOCKFILE_BYTES = 16_777_216, MAX_DEPENDENCY_PACKAGES = MAX_IMPORT_ENTRIES - 1.
- dependencyError(code), mirroring snapshotError. It holds a MESSAGES table of fixed text for DEPENDENCY_INPUT_INVALID, DEPENDENCY_LOCKFILE_INVALID, DEPENDENCY_LOCATION_INVALID, DEPENDENCY_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED, DEPENDENCY_INTEGRITY_INVALID and DEPENDENCY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. An unknown code becomes DEPENDENCY_INPUT_INVALID. An OWN_ERRORS WeakSet marks errors made here.
- admitLockfiles(input). Inside try/catch, any error not in OWN_ERRORS becomes DEPENDENCY_INPUT_INVALID, so there is never a partial result.

admitLockfiles steps:
1. Input. isRecord(input), as in source-snapshot.mjs (prototype Object.prototype or null), and Reflect.ownKeys exactly {lockfiles, cpu}. Read cpu once; it must be 'x64' or 'arm64'.
   Read lockfiles once. It must satisfy Array.isArray, have prototype Array.prototype, and a length read ONCE that is an integer from 1 to MAX_LOCKFILES. Read each element once by index.
   Each element is an exact-key {dir, bytes} record, and each is read once:
   - dir is '.' or validateImportPath(dir) === dir. A snapshot error becomes DEPENDENCY_INPUT_INVALID.
   - Duplicate dir strings are refused.
   - bytes passes ArrayBuffer.isView, with prototype Uint8Array.prototype or Buffer.prototype.
   - Its size comes from the intrinsic %TypedArray% byteLength getter, as source-snapshot's viewLength, so it cannot be spoofed. A size over MAX_LOCKFILE_BYTES is DEPENDENCY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, checked BEFORE decoding.
2. Lockfile. Decode with new TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal: true}), which strips a BOM by default, then JSON.parse. The value must be a plain object with lockfileVersion === 2 or 3 and packages a plain object. Otherwise it is DEPENDENCY_LOCKFILE_INVALID.
3. For each [key, entry] of Object.entries(packages), in this order:
   a. key '' is skipped.
   b. LOCATION = new RegExp(`^node_modules/(?:${NAME}/node_modules/)*(${NAME})$`), where NAME = `(?:@[A-Za-z0-9~-][A-Za-z0-9._~-]*/)?[A-Za-z0-9~-][A-Za-z0-9._~-]*`.
      NAME's character class excludes '/', so the regex has no ambiguous nesting and runs in linear time. Its last capture is the location's name. A miss is DEPENDENCY_LOCATION_INVALID.
   c. entry must be a plain object, else DEPENDENCY_LOCKFILE_INVALID.
   d. entry.inBundle === true is skipped.
   e. entry.optional === true is skipped when !passes('linux', entry.os) or !passes(cpu, entry.cpu).
      passes copies npm-install-checks checkList:
      - undefined passes;
      - a string becomes [string];
      - anything that is not an array of strings passes, so it is never a reason to skip;
      - ['any'] passes;
      - any matching '!x' fails;
      - otherwise it passes on a positive match, or when every entry is negated.
      libc is never consulted.
   f. entry.link === true is DEPENDENCY_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED.
   g. name is entry.name if it is present, else the captured location name. It must fully match NAME.
      version must be a string matching ^(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)(?:-[0-9A-Za-z-]+(?:\.[0-9A-Za-z-]+)*)?(?:\+[0-9A-Za-z-]+(?:\.[0-9A-Za-z-]+)*)?$.
      resolved must === `https://registry.npmjs.org/${name}/-/${name.slice(name.lastIndexOf('/') + 1)}-${version}.tgz`: plain string equality, no URL parsing.
      Any miss is DEPENDENCY_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED.
   h. integrity must match ^sha512-([A-Za-z0-9+/]{86}==)$, and Buffer.from(b64, 'base64').toString('base64') === b64 (canonical text). Else DEPENDENCY_INTEGRITY_INVALID. sha512 is the decoded hex.
   i. Deduplicate in a Map keyed by sha512, keeping the smaller url. When the map's size passes MAX_DEPENDENCY_PACKAGES, throw DEPENDENCY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED at once.
4. Result:
   - dirs sorted by Buffer.compare of their UTF-8 bytes;
   - packages as frozen {integrity, sha512, url} records, sorted by sha512;
   - the arrays and the result frozen.
   Return Object.freeze({dirs, packages}).

Error handling: every refusal is a dependencyError with fixed text, never input bytes, a URL, a key or a path. Getters, Proxies and hostile values can only produce DEPENDENCY_INPUT_INVALID. The function writes nothing, fetches nothing, and spawns nothing.
implementationPlan.note: Created dependency-cache.mjs (pure admitLockfiles/dependencyError + 3 constants; imports only ./source-snapshot.mjs). DA1-DA5 green. Deviation from plan wording only in structure: each lockfile is size-bounded, decoded, parsed and its entries folded into the shared Map inside the per-element loop, so a later getter cannot mutate already-read bytes and only one parsed lockfile is live at a time; refusals and codes are unchanged. Probed 19 mutants (fatal decode, canonical re-encode, smallest-url, inBundle, os/cpu filter, negation, intrinsic byteLength, UTF-8 dir order, sha512 order, count bounds, link, dup dir, alias name, root skip, freeze, prototype checks); all killed except the dir round-trip compare, which is an equivalent mutant (validateImportPath returns its input).

implementationPlan.description:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, as the final step. Load adversarial-self-review and read the two-file diff as an attacker:
- Can any lockfile entry make npm write outside node_modules once it is admitted? Try '..', '.', backslashes, empty segments, a scope without a name, percent-encoding, and a workspace folder key.
- Can a non-registry or non-canonical source pass? Try a case change, a port, userinfo, a query or fragment, an alias pointing at another package's tarball, or a version mismatch. Can a skipped entry (root, inBundle, optional) smuggle anything into packages?
- Can two integrity texts name the same bytes (non-canonical base64), or a multi-hash slip through?
- Is each input property read once, so a getter or Proxy cannot pass validation and then change? Is the lockfile size bound checked BEFORE decoding?
- Is every regex linear? Time a 1 MB hostile key once, by hand, outside the suite.
- Does any message carry input text?
- Is the result deterministic and deeply frozen?
- Would I be embarrassed if this shipped?
Fix any finding, then re-run step 3's command fresh before complete_task.
implementationPlan.note: Self-review found one REAL defect and fixed it. (1) FIXED: the plan skipped inBundle/optional entries BEFORE the link check. I reproduced with npm 12.2.0 in a throwaway dir that `npm ci --offline --ignore-scripts` still creates node_modules/evil -> ../target for {link:true,inBundle:true}; a later admitted key node_modules/evil/node_modules/x would then extract under the link target, outside node_modules. The link refusal now runs before both skips (comment + header updated), and two DA3 rows ({link,inBundle} and {link,optional,os:darwin}) fail against the old order (mutant run: DA3 fails) and pass now. This deviates from the plan's literal "inBundle never checked further" and is the only deviation; plain inBundle entries are still skipped (DA4). (2) Checked, no finding: hostile 1 MB keys/names/versions/integrity/resolved (long name, nested segments, scoped repeats, 66k-deep valid key) all resolve in 1-12 ms, so every regex is linear; a 16 MiB lockfile of '[' is refused LOCKFILE_INVALID in ~750 ms / ~430 MB RSS, bounded by MAX_LOCKFILE_BYTES with one parsed lockfile live at a time; size is checked before decoding via the intrinsic byteLength getter; each input property is read once (spy test); no message carries input text; result is deterministic and deeply frozen. Repo lockfiles: daemon 88 and proxy 46 packages admitted for x64 and arm64, vscode 298 admitted, claude-plugin refused DEPENDENCY_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED (known, out of scope). (3) Theoretical, left for R11e3/e5: the lockfile entries are constrained but package.json (candidate-controlled) still shapes the install, including workspaces; a 66k-deep valid location passes admission and only npm's own path limit refuses it; two lockfiles can name one URL with different integrity (R11e3's download verification fails closed); dir aliasing on case-insensitive names is caught later by validateImport's foldCase collision check. Fresh final run: exit 0, 33 pass / 1 skip (K9, pre-existing) / 0 fail; size 142 + 145 = 287 lines. source-export.mjs shows modified in git status; it is a peer's change, untouched by this task.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: admitLockfiles({lockfiles, cpu}) deterministically turns 1-16 untrusted npm lockfiles (v2/v3) into the frozen, deduplicated list of canonical registry.npmjs.org tarballs with sha512 integrity that the host may fetch. It skips root, bundled and platform-excluded optional entries, and refuses every other entry kind with a fixed DEPENDENCY_* code before anything is downloaded.
acceptanceCriteria: DA1-DA5 pass under the verification command.
invariants: No I/O in admitLockfiles' call graph.
Each input property is read once.
compatibility: The E, K and C rows are unchanged.
CQ-R11e3 consumes {dirs, packages:[{integrity, sha512, url}]} exactly.
approvedScope: scripts/local-runner/dependency-cache.mjs (new): admitLockfiles, dependencyError, MAX_LOCKFILES, MAX_LOCKFILE_BYTES, MAX_DEPENDENCY_PACKAGES

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Split from CQ-R11e3 by SPIDR Interface: admission here, and download, tree and the npm end-to-end row in R11e3. Rejected alternatives:
- A separate lockfile-admission.mjs module. The task description and its consumers name dependency-cache.mjs, and R11e3 extends that same module.
- An import-purity test row. R11e3 legitimately adds fs and the downloader import to this module, and such a row would force R11e3 to weaken a DA row. QA checks DoD 4's import clause by reading this slice.
- URL parsing to compare resolved. Plain equality with the canonical template is stricter and has no normalization tricks.
- Filtering on libc. An extra package is harmless; a missing one breaks the offline install.
- Skipping devOptional entries. npm only skips platform-excluded packages that are optional.
planningNotes.risks:
- NAME's first character excludes '.' and '_' in both the scope and the name.
- The scoped name inside a location ('node_modules/@s/b') must stay one capture. Do not derive the name with lastIndexOf('node_modules/'), because a scope named '@node_modules' breaks that.
- Non-canonical base64: Buffer.from(...,'base64') is lenient, so the canonical re-encode comparison is required.
- Generating 10,000 entries (DA5) takes about 2.3 MB of JSON. Keep it out of the per-row loops.
- Never write the double-underscore proto literal or an eval call in code or tests: they are global forbidden patterns.
- A BOM is tolerated, which matches npm.

completionSummary: Added scripts/local-runner/dependency-cache.mjs (142 lines, new): pure, network-free admitLockfiles({lockfiles, cpu}), dependencyError(code) with six fixed DEPENDENCY_* messages, and MAX_LOCKFILES=16 / MAX_LOCKFILE_BYTES=16_777_216 / MAX_DEPENDENCY_PACKAGES=MAX_IMPORT_ENTRIES-1. It imports only ./source-snapshot.mjs (no fs/net/child_process). It returns a deeply frozen {dirs (UTF-8 sorted), packages:[{integrity, sha512, url}] (one per distinct integrity, smallest canonical url, sorted by sha512)}. Registry-only: resolved must equal the canonical https://registry.npmjs.org tarball URL by plain string equality, with one canonical sha512 SRI (re-encode check). Root and inBundle entries are skipped; optional entries are skipped when os excludes linux or cpu excludes the given cpu (checkList semantics, libc never filtered). Everything else refuses with a fixed code; size is bounded before decoding with the intrinsic byteLength getter; each property is read once. Tests DA1-DA5 (+145 lines) in scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs; E/K/C rows untouched. 19+ mutants probed and killed. ONE DEVIATION from the plan text, found in self-review: the link refusal runs BEFORE the inBundle/optional skips, because npm 12.2.0 was shown to still create the symlink for a link entry flagged inBundle, which a later nested key could write through; two DA3 rows pin it.
